slides.0.title: Industry, Market and Trade
slides.0.subtitle: Structure, exports and recent change
slides.1.title: Scale and structure
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Vineyards and output
slides.1.highlights.0.content: About 64,020 ha of wine-grape vineyard in July 2022; about 2.1 million hl produced in 2022, 19th in the world
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Falling output
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Output fell about 14% in 2022–23, a multi-decade low; about 296 ha of vineyard was abandoned that year
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Bulk wine is half the domestic market
slides.1.highlights.2.content: About 50% of the Greek market is bulk or non-standard wine
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Low protected-wine share
slides.1.highlights.3.content: PDO + PGI is about a third of output, far below other EU producers
slides.1.content: Figures come largely from the Ministry via KEOSOE (2023) and OIV; give the year and source when citing.
slides.2.title: Exports and key markets
slides.2.highlights.0.title: 2023 export value
slides.2.highlights.0.content: About €99.7 million (about €99 million in 2022); volume 28,853 tonnes, slightly below roughly 29,900 tonnes in 2022
slides.2.highlights.1.title: The EU takes 86.6%
slides.2.highlights.1.content: 86.6% of export value goes to the EU; the top five markets are Germany, Cyprus, France, the Netherlands and Belgium
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Value grew faster than volume
slides.2.highlights.2.content: In 2022 export value grew about 16.8% against about 6.6% for volume, read as rising share and prices
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Trade-show visibility
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Greece's ProWein 2023 pavilion had a record 64 participants
slides.2.content: Export concentration in the EU is both an opportunity (close, familiar) and a risk (high dependence).
slides.3.title: Quality shift and price positioning
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Island scarcity
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Santorini grapes cost more than ten times the northern Greek price, reflecting scarcity and collapsed yields
slides.3.highlights.1.title: A new generation of producers
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Boutique estates use native grapes and better base wines (as in modern Retsina)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Tourism cuts both ways
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Tourism brings brand and sales, but also pressure on land and labour (as on Paros)
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Main challenges
slides.3.highlights.3.content: Climate change, brand recognition, a low protected-wine share and the weight of bulk wine
slides.3.content: Essay template: structure (high bulk share) → shift (boutique, native grapes) → market (EU dependence) → risks (climate, yield).
